title: Interest Days on Member Appeals to Out-of-Network Plans Paying First — Insurance Coverage & Claims Timetable
content:
**Timetable — Insurance Coverage & Claims, member appeals to an out-of-network plan that pays first.** The first-plan member appeal's interest days run as follows, the plan's adjudication time being the calendar days between the claim's filing date and its denial date (the latest denial date on the claim), and the expected adjudication days being those of the coverage's payer class:

| Plan's adjudication time | Interest days |
|---|---|
| More than twice the expected adjudication days | Every calendar day from the filing date to today |
| More than the expected adjudication days, not more than twice | Calendar days from the filing date to today, less the expected adjudication days |
| Not more than the expected adjudication days | None |

## Expected adjudication days by payer class

| Payer class | Expected adjudication period (calendar days of filing) | More than this | More than twice this |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Medicare Supplement Plan | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial In-Network Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | 45 | 46 or more days | 91 or more days |

## Worked days (hypothetical Commercial Out-of-Network Plan claim filed 120 days ago)

- Denied 91 days after filing: more than twice 45, so 120 interest days.
- Denied 90 days after filing: more than 45 but not more than 90, so 120 less 45, 75 interest days.
- Denied 46 days after filing: 75 interest days.
- Denied 45 days after filing: none.
